title: Design a Databricks Lakehouse (Medallion + Delta) and Defend It

teaser.setup: You own the data platform. The business wants trustworthy analytics on Databricks fed by batch and streaming sources. Design the lakehouse and defend the calls under pressure — medallion layering, Delta reliability, performance, cost, and governance.
you_will_practice: Idempotent incremental loads and schema evolution
Unity Catalog governance and cluster cost control

sample_node.prompt: Why land raw in bronze instead of transforming before load?
sample_node.model: Raw bronze is an immutable, replayable source of truth: when transformation logic changes you reprocess from bronze without re-ingesting, and transforms run on elastic Spark close to the data. Trade-off: more storage and a larger governance surface. For strict PII-at-source you'd mask on ingest and accept less replayability.

n1.prompt: Clarify first, then give your one-paragraph lakehouse design for batch + streaming analytics on Databricks.
n1.model: Clarify: volume/velocity, per-table freshness SLO, event ordering/dedup, PII, and a cost ceiling. Design: medallion on Delta — bronze (raw, replayable) → silver (cleaned/conformed) → gold (business marts); batch via incremental MERGE, streaming via Structured Streaming into bronze; data-quality gates between layers; Unity Catalog for governance/lineage; freshness + cost monitoring. Serve gold to BI.

n2.prompt: Why land raw in bronze instead of transforming before load?
n2.model: Raw bronze is an immutable, replayable source of truth: when logic changes you reprocess from bronze without re-ingesting, and transforms run on elastic Spark close to the data. Trade-off: more storage and a larger governance surface. For strict PII-at-source you'd mask on ingest and accept less replayability.

n3.prompt: A streaming job is retried after a partial failure. How do you avoid duplicates or corruption in Delta?
n3.model: Idempotent writes: MERGE on a stable business key for batch; for streaming use checkpointed exactly-once sinks so a replay doesn't double-write. Backfills target a bounded window with the same merge logic. A retried run converges to the same table state — safe by design, not luck. Delta's ACID transactions prevent partial-commit corruption.
signals: MERGE on business key / exactly-once checkpointing
relies on Delta ACID, not append-and-hope

n4.prompt: An upstream source adds and renames columns without warning. How does your pipeline survive it?
n4.model: Bronze is schema-tolerant with Delta schema evolution/mergeSchema so new columns are additive, never a crash. Pin the silver/gold contract to the columns you actually consume and map explicitly, so an upstream rename surfaces as a controlled mapping change, not silent loss. Version the schema and alert on unexpected changes. Additive-safe at the edge, contract-stable in the middle.

n5.prompt: Analysts must only see rows for their region, and PII must be masked. How do you enforce it on the lakehouse?
n5.model: Govern in Unity Catalog: table/column grants, column-masking functions for PII, and row-level filters by region tied to the user's group. Enforce at the data layer so every tool/BI client inherits it — never rely on the dashboard to filter. Lineage + audit so access is reviewable.
signals: Unity Catalog grants + column masking + row filters
enforced at the data layer, inherited by all clients

n6.prompt: A Spark job that was fast is now slow and spilling after data growth. Diagnose it.
n6.model: Read the Spark UI stages. Usual suspects: data skew on a join/group key (one lagging task), small-file explosion from streaming (OPTIMIZE/compaction + auto-optimize), shuffle spill from under-partitioning or an undersized cluster, or an exploding join from a grain bug. Fix the specific cause — salt/repartition the skewed key, compact, tune shuffle partitions, Z-ORDER/liquid-cluster the filter columns. Don't just upsize to hide skew.
signals: doesn't just upsize to mask skew

n7.prompt: Databricks cost doubled this month. Find and fix it without hurting SLAs.
n7.model: Attribute cost: all-purpose clusters used for jobs (move to job clusters), idle/oversized clusters (autoscaling + auto-termination), inefficient queries (the Spark perf fixes above), and over-frequent streaming where batch would do. Use spot/fleet where interruption is tolerable. Measure $/job and set budgets/alerts. Cut waste first, then right-size — keep the freshness SLOs intact.
signals: job clusters not all-purpose; autoscale + auto-terminate

n8.prompt: Where did you assert a choice without the mechanism, the trade-off, or the verification?
checklist: I justified medallion layering (replayability) with its trade-off
I made retries idempotent (MERGE/checkpoint), not append-and-hope
I handled schema evolution with a stable consumed contract
I governed access in Unity Catalog at the data layer
I diagnosed Spark perf by cause and cut cost without breaking SLOs

recommend.label: Keep Asking Why — data platform chain
